sections.name: Intent
sections.summary: The outcomes the product exists for.

requirements.text: WYSIWYG markdown editor + folder tree
requirements.story: Users write in a WYSIWYG markdown editor and organize docs in folders

requirements.text: MCP: agents search/read/write/script over all docs
requirements.story: Agents can search, read, edit, and script across all your docs

requirements.text: Cloud storage; .md and .pdf download
requirements.story: Docs live in the cloud and download as .md or .pdf

requirements.text: Full git-backed history; one commit per accepted change
requirements.backing: USER; 40 ms p95 commit, +700 KB/1000 saves MEASURED
requirements.story: Every change is kept in version history

requirements.text: Snappy; Rust only where it measurably helps
requirements.story: Everything feels instant

requirements.text: Google sign-in
requirements.story: Users sign in with Google

requirements.text: MCP OAuth (ChatGPT accepts only OAuth)
requirements.story: Agents connect through an OAuth sign-in, including from claude.ai and ChatGPT

requirements.text: Simplest merge: CAS + editor overwrite (every version committed)
requirements.story: A stale agent edit is rejected; your editor's edit wins, and nothing is lost

requirements.text: Image paste/drag
requirements.story: Users can paste or drag images into docs

sections.name: Storage & history
sections.summary: git is the authority; docs/ is a checkout projection.

requirements.text: Per-account tokio Mutex around Store::apply
requirements.story: Edits to one account are applied one at a time

edit.why: ~100 LOC of types at 20 LOC/min = 5, plus 5 designing a contract every lane builds on.

build_test.why: One compile-and-test cycle (3 min).

verify.why: Read the signatures against their callers in R18, R27, R28.

scope.basis: ~100 LOC of types: Store::apply, Mutation, Writer, error enum, per-account Mutex map.
scope.risk: Low; it's a contract, but every lane waits on it.

requirements.text: Path identity; 422 invalid names; 409 when equal after NFC + case folding; reserved `_assets`
requirements.backing: ~160 LOC; zip collision loss MEASURED r3
requirements.story: Doc names are validated, and names that clash only by case are refused

edit.why: ~160 LOC (validator + table tests) at 20 LOC/min.

build_test.why: Two compile-and-test cycles; Unicode edge cases usually fail once.

verify.why: Check the NFC/NFD and case pair against the APFS behavior measured in round 3.

scope.basis: ~160 LOC name validation with NFC normalization + case folding, plus table tests.
scope.risk: Unicode case-folding edge cases (ß, dotted/dotless i).

requirements.text: Commit from memory (blob + changed subtrees + HEAD; author = writer) with GIT_OPT_ENABLE_FSYNC_GITDIR; identical bytes → return rev, no commit; then write docs/ file. Startup per account before serving: delete stale *.lock, checkout_head force + remove_untracked, fsck --connectivity-only, gc --auto
requirements.backing: ~240 LOC; save p95 17 ms; checkout 25 ms–1.3 s; fsck 0.05 s MEASURED
requirements.story: A save is durable in history before it's acknowledged

edit.why: ~240 LOC at 20 LOC/min = 12, plus 3 porting the round-3 and round-5 spike code.

build_test.why: ~3 cycles at 3 min; the 4 crash-state fixtures and the stale-lock test are the slow ones.

verify.why: Rerun the round-3 benchmark: 300 saves on a 10k-doc repo, p95 against 100 ms.

scope.basis: ~240 LOC: blob write, changed-subtree rebuild, HEAD update, gitdir fsync option, identical-bytes no-op, startup recovery. Spiked in rounds 3 and 5.
scope.risk: Unsafe libgit2_sys option call; nested-path subtree rebuild; 4 crash-state tests to write.

requirements.text: Bare repo at /data/accounts/<id>/git (init_bare) opened with set_workdir(docs/, false): no .git file/dir in docs/, no core.worktree; shell git uses --git-dir/--work-tree
requirements.story: Your doc folder contains only your files, never git internals

edit.why: ~20 LOC, copied from the round-5 spike.

build_test.why: One short cycle with the 'no .git in docs/' test.

verify.why: Covered by the R55 test.

scope.basis: init_bare + set_workdir and one test asserting no .git in docs/. Spiked in round 5.
scope.risk: Low.

requirements.text: Durable commit before ack (gitdir fsync); editor resends unacked buffer; startup checkout+fsck; volume backups
requirements.story: No acknowledged edit is lost after a crash or restart

requirements.text: Doc ≤ 5 MB UTF-8
requirements.story: A single doc can be up to 5 MB

edit.why: ~25 LOC: size check, 413 error.

build_test.why: One cycle.

verify.why: Covered by its unit test.

scope.basis: Size check, 413 error, one test.
scope.risk: Low.

sections.name: Search
sections.summary: Disposable FTS5 index for search and listing.

requirements.text: FTS5 via docmap(path PK → rowid); search + listing only; rebuilt unconditionally at startup
requirements.backing: ~140 LOC; upsert 0.34 ms; rebuild 0.7 s MEASURED
requirements.story: Search returns ranked results with snippets instantly

edit.why: ~140 LOC at 20 LOC/min = 7, plus 5 designing FTS5 query escaping for user input.

build_test.why: ~2.5 cycles, including generating the 10k-doc fixture.

verify.why: Query p95 against the 20 ms budget with the round-1 corpus generator.

scope.basis: ~140 LOC: docmap + FTS5 schema, upsert by rowid, bm25 + snippet query, folder/date filters, startup rebuild. Spiked in rounds 1 and 3.
scope.risk: User query syntax must be escaped for FTS5 MATCH.

sections.name: Scripting
sections.summary: The filesystem is the script API; one commit per applied run.

requirements.text: Filesystem is the script API: /docs overlay with full file + directory ops; final /docs state = change set; empty dirs dropped and reported; mtimes = last commit time; docs.search optional; history not mounted; dry_run diffs; one commit per applied run
requirements.backing: Engineer: files exposed to scripts as a filesystem as much as possible; file ops spiked r2
requirements.short: capturing folder ops (mkdir/rename dir) in scripts
requirements.story: Agent scripts work on your docs as ordinary files and folders

edit.why: ~380 LOC at 20 LOC/min = 19, plus 6 porting the round-2 capture spike (100 lines).

build_test.why: ~3 cycles at 3 min; each test starts a Monty worker.

verify.why: Run 3 representative agent scripts end to end: bulk rename, regex rewrite, read-only report.

scope.basis: ~380 LOC: pool setup, overlay mount, OsCall capture, postlude, similar diffs, Batch build, mtimes, empty-dir drop. Capture spiked in round 2.
scope.risk: Postlude / result= convention and PosixPath parsing are new glue.

requirements.text: Capture directory ops (mkdir, rmdir, dir rename) through monty-fs and turn dir renames into per-document moves
requirements.backing: UNVERIFIED: round 2 spiked file ops only; first spike in W7
requirements.story: Scripts can create, remove, and rename folders

edit.why: ~50 LOC to turn directory renames into per-document moves.

build_test.why: The spike itself: a minimal Monty run of mkdir / rmdir / rename on an overlay mount (same size as the round-2 spike).

verify.why: Covered by the R55 folder-rename test.

scope.basis: 10-min spike of mkdir/rmdir/dir-rename through monty-fs, then wiring dir renames to per-document moves.
scope.risk: Largest unknown in scripting: if monty-fs doesn't route dir ops, deriving renames from the file diff adds ~20 min.

requirements.text: Limits: 30 s, 256 MB, 50 MB overlay, max_suspensions 1 000 000, 1 MB stdout
requirements.story: A runaway script is stopped by time and memory limits

edit.why: ~20 LOC of ResourceLimits config and a stdout cap.

build_test.why: One cycle; each limit test fails fast by design.

verify.why: Covered by its tests.

scope.basis: Monty ResourceLimits config + stdout cap in the print callback; one test per limit.
scope.risk: Low.

requirements.text: monty-pool subprocess isolation
requirements.story: A crashing script can't take down the server

requirements.text: Warm script start < 5 ms
requirements.story: Scripts start instantly

sections.name: MCP & auth
sections.summary: AuthKit is the OAuth server; rdocs validates tokens and serves 8 tools.

requirements.text: Email allowlist `ALLOWED_EMAILS`; per-account private repo keyed by WorkOS user id
requirements.short: email allowlist instead of open sign-up (overrides your call)
requirements.story: Only allowlisted emails can sign in

edit.why: ~25 LOC: parse ALLOWED_EMAILS, check it in two places.

build_test.why: One cycle with a 403 test.

verify.why: Covered by R55.

scope.basis: Parse ALLOWED_EMAILS, check in the login callback and MCP middleware, 403 test.
scope.risk: Low.

requirements.text: WorkOS AuthKit: Google, CIMD + DCR, JWKS, resource indicator, identity linking. Work: WorkOS dashboard config (Google connection, CIMD + DCR, resource indicator); human gate.
requirements.story: Sign-in and agent authorization flow through WorkOS AuthKit with Google

edit.why: Write a ~30-line setup checklist for the WorkOS dashboard.

build_test.why: Nothing to build.

verify.why: curl both discovery endpoints and confirm the CIMD and DCR toggles. Your dashboard time isn't counted.

scope.basis: Write the WorkOS setup checklist and verify the discovery endpoints once configured. The dashboard work itself is a human gate and isn't counted.
scope.risk: Waits on you: Google OAuth client, CIMD + DCR toggles, resource indicator.

requirements.text: Encrypted cookie session {account_id, expires}; 30-day rolling. Includes the AuthKit code exchange on /login callback.
requirements.story: Users stay signed in for 30 days

edit.why: ~200 LOC at 20 LOC/min = 10, plus 5 reading the WorkOS auth API (there's no Rust SDK).

build_test.why: Two cycles for cookie and expiry tests.

verify.why: One local login against WorkOS if R11 is configured; otherwise it moves to the R55 smoke.

scope.basis: AuthKit code exchange over HTTP (no Rust SDK), PrivateCookieJar session, 30-day rolling expiry.
scope.risk: WorkOS API shapes read from docs; only proven end-to-end in the real smoke test.

requirements.text: 401 + protected-resource metadata; AS metadata proxy; JWT (JWKS, aud, exp, allowlist); writer name = client_id via known-clients map, fallback host
requirements.story: Agent requests are authenticated, and each edit is credited to the agent that made it

edit.why: ~150 LOC at 20 LOC/min = 8, plus 4 re-reading the protected-resource metadata spec.

build_test.why: ~2.5 cycles; tests sign tokens with a local key.

verify.why: Real-token check happens in the R55 smoke.

scope.basis: ~150 LOC: protected-resource metadata, AS metadata proxy, JWKS cache, JWT validation, client_id → writer name; tests with locally signed tokens.
scope.risk: client_id claim shape unconfirmed until a real Claude Code token is decoded.

requirements.text: 8 MCP tools via rmcp: list, search, read, history(list/show via git CLI --follow) [readOnlyHint] + save, move (folder move = Batch), delete, run_script; restore = save old content
requirements.story: Agents get 8 tools; read-only ones can be auto-approved

edit.why: ~520 LOC at 20 LOC/min = 26; the 8 handlers are thin wrappers and rmcp macros generate the schemas.

build_test.why: ~3 cycles of the rmcp-client integration harness.

verify.why: Connect Claude Code locally and call each tool once.

scope.basis: ~520 LOC: 8 tool schemas + handlers over store, search, history, scripts via rmcp; rmcp-client integration tests.
scope.risk: rmcp macro API churn between versions.

requirements.text: Google cannot be MCP AS → AuthKit
requirements.story: Agents authorize through AuthKit because Google can't issue MCP tokens

sections.name: Web client
sections.summary: One TS bundle: SolidJS shell + Milkdown kit editor.

requirements.text: One Vite TS bundle: SolidJS shell + @milkdown/kit (commonmark, gfm, listener, history, clipboard, upload). Includes the SolidJS shell: folder tree (create, rename, drag, delete), ⌘K palette, download menu.
requirements.story: Users get a folder tree, search palette, and editor in one small bundle

edit.why: ~800 LOC TS at 25 LOC/min = 32, plus 8 for layout and interaction design.

build_test.why: ~10 Vite + vitest cycles at about 1 min each.

verify.why: Drive the tree by hand in a browser: create, rename, drag, delete, palette. UI checks are slow.

scope.basis: ~800 LOC TS: Solid shell, folder tree (create, rename, drag, delete), context menu, ⌘K palette, API client; verified by driving it in a browser.
scope.risk: No measured history for Solid UI work; drag-and-drop tree is the usual time sink.

requirements.text: Editor reconcile: narrow replace via findDiffStart/End (ignore heading ids), keep selection; dirty → overwrite with notice + Restore
requirements.story: An agent's edit appears in your open doc without moving your cursor

edit.why: ~40 LOC = 2, plus 6 working through ProseMirror diff and selection mapping (spiked in round 2).

build_test.why: ~7 quick test cycles over headings, tables, and lists.

verify.why: Covered by the R55 'agent save while open' journey.

scope.basis: ~40 LOC narrow replace with selection mapping, ignoring heading ids. Spiked in round 2.
scope.risk: Selection mapping across complex nodes (tables, lists).

requirements.text: Images: account-root `_assets/<git-blob-id>.<ext>`, root-relative links; png/jpeg/gif/webp ≤ 20 MB; no SVG. Includes paste/drag upload in the editor.
requirements.story: Users can paste or drag images, and they survive doc moves

edit.why: ~150 LOC Rust + TS at 20 LOC/min.

build_test.why: Two Rust cycles plus one TS cycle.

verify.why: Covered by the R55 image-paste journey.

scope.basis: Upload endpoint with type/size checks and blob-id naming, Milkdown upload plugin wiring.
scope.risk: Low.

requirements.text: History drawer: commit list grouped by writer, jsdiff diffWordsWithSpace, Restore button, deleted-doc list. Includes server history reads (git CLI log --follow, show, deleted list) used by both the drawer and the MCP history tool.
requirements.story: Users can browse a doc's history, see word-level diffs, and restore

edit.why: Rust history reads ~150 LOC at 20 LOC/min = 7.5; TS drawer ~250 LOC at 25 LOC/min = 10; plus 5 reading git log output formats and 5 designing the same-writer grouping.

build_test.why: 3 Rust cycles at 3 min plus 6 TS cycles at 1 min.

verify.why: Browse a 1,000-commit history in the browser, restore a version, restore a deleted doc.

scope.basis: Server history reads (git CLI log --follow / show / deleted list, ~150 LOC Rust, 30 min) + drawer (commit list, same-writer grouping, jsdiff word diffs, restore, deleted list, ~250 LOC TS, 40 min).
scope.risk: On the critical path; splitting server reads from the drawer would let the MCP history tool and the drawer run in parallel. git CLI output parsing.

requirements.text: Autosave 500 ms / ≥ 5 s; one boot request; hover prefetch LRU
requirements.story: Docs autosave and open instantly

edit.why: ~100 LOC at 25 LOC/min = 4, plus 6 for the timing logic (debounce, max interval, LRU).

build_test.why: Fake-timer unit tests, ~5 cycles.

verify.why: Covered by R56 cold-load and R55 journeys.

scope.basis: Autosave debounce + max interval, boot request, hover-prefetch LRU.
scope.risk: Low.

requirements.text: Unreachable server → banner; EventSource auto-reconnect → tree refetch
requirements.story: Users see a clear banner when the server is unreachable

edit.why: ~30 LOC banner bound to EventSource state.

build_test.why: One test toggling the connection.

verify.why: Covered by R55.

scope.basis: Banner bound to EventSource state.
scope.risk: Low.

requirements.text: SSE per account: one `changed {commit, writer, paths[], tab_id}` event
requirements.story: Open tabs learn about other writers' changes right away

edit.why: ~60 LOC Rust + ~40 LOC TS = 5, plus 5 settling reconnect and tab_id semantics.

build_test.why: Two Rust cycles plus an EventSource test.

verify.why: Two browser tabs: confirm the event arrives and the tab_id echo is ignored.

scope.basis: Per-account broadcast channel, cookie-authenticated SSE endpoint, tab_id echo.
scope.risk: Low.

requirements.text: One in-flight save per doc, base = last ack rev; dirty = buffer ≠ last ack content (in-flight counts); 409 handled as remote change (overwrite_of); tab_id echoed and own events ignored
requirements.story: Typing never triggers a false "overwrote changes" notice

edit.why: ~60 LOC = 2.5, plus 2.5 settling the dirty and in-flight state.

build_test.why: Unit tests on the save queue; the Playwright cases are counted in R55.

verify.why: Covered by R55.

scope.basis: One-in-flight queue, dirty definition, 409 → overwrite path. Its Playwright cases are counted in R55.
scope.risk: Race bugs show up only in end-to-end tests.

requirements.text: JS editor (no mature Rust WYSIWYG)
requirements.story: Agents build the editor on Milkdown since no mature Rust WYSIWYG exists

requirements.text: remark vs pulldown-cmark divergence → corpus test
requirements.story: PDFs render the same markdown the editor shows

edit.why: Grow the round-2 corpus from 11 to ~20 docs and write a ~40-line compare script.

build_test.why: Run it and triage the differences.

verify.why: The script is the check.

scope.basis: ~20-document corpus and a script comparing remark output with pulldown-cmark rendering.
scope.risk: Divergences found may need stringify-option changes (R51′).

requirements.text: Never save on open; remark stringify options match agent conventions (`-` bullets, ATX, inline links)
requirements.story: Opening a doc never rewrites it, and edits change as little markdown as possible

edit.why: Stringify options plus a no-save-on-open guard.

build_test.why: One test asserting open produces no save.

verify.why: Covered by R50's corpus.

scope.basis: remark stringify options + a no-save-on-open guard and test.
scope.risk: Low.

requirements.text: Web export: .md bytes; .zip (account-root paths + referenced assets); .pdf via md2pdf-core; merman pinned
requirements.story: Users can download a doc or folder as .md, .zip, or .pdf

edit.why: ~120 LOC at 20 LOC/min = 6, plus 9 reading the md2pdf-core API and streaming-zip examples.

build_test.why: md2pdf/Typst compile ≈ 1 min, plus 2 cycles at 3 min plus fixes.

verify.why: Open the generated .md, .zip, and .pdf by hand and check images and filenames (3 formats).

scope.basis: md bytes, streamed zip with referenced assets, md2pdf-core call with root-relative images.
scope.risk: Young crate (209 downloads) with a merman pin; image path resolution.

requirements.text: ~10-page PDF < 500 ms
requirements.story: PDFs generate in under half a second

sections.name: Deploy & operations
sections.summary: One Railway service, one volume with scheduled backups.

requirements.text: One Rust axum binary owns /data: API, SSE, MCP, static assets; rmcp allowed_hosts = public host
requirements.story: Agents deploy one binary that serves the app, API, and MCP

edit.why: ~200 LOC at 20 LOC/min = 10, plus 2 wiring embedded static assets.

build_test.why: Two cycles, one fixing route tests.

verify.why: curl each route once.

scope.basis: axum router, JSON handlers, embedded static assets from the Vite build.
scope.risk: Low.

requirements.text: Docker (cargo-chef; Vite stage; Monty worker binary; git CLI for gc/fsck) → Railway service + volume (backups on); rust-toolchain ≥ 1.98
requirements.story: Agents ship with a single container deploy to Railway

edit.why: ~150 lines of config at 10 lines/min = 15, plus 10 reading the Monty, cargo-chef, and Railway docs.

build_test.why: First cold build of the workspace: vendored libgit2, Typst (md2pdf alone took 58 s in round 1), Monty ≈ 5; first cold Docker image build ≈ 10.

verify.why: Run check.sh green and boot the container locally against /healthz.

scope.basis: Config only (~150 lines): Cargo workspace, rust-toolchain.toml, scripts/check.sh, Dockerfile with cargo-chef, Vite stage, Monty worker binary, git CLI.
scope.risk: First cold build is slow (md2pdf alone compiled in 58 s in round 1); Monty needs rustc ≥ 1.98, so the toolchain must be installed first.

requirements.text: Railway scheduled volume backups (daily 6 d, weekly 27 d, monthly 89 d); one manual restore in test env before launch
requirements.backing: config; same-provider risk flagged to engineer
requirements.short: backups only on Railway, or also off-provider?
requirements.story: The volume is backed up daily, weekly, and monthly

edit.why: One Railway CLI/API call to set the schedule.

build_test.why: Nothing to build.

verify.why: Confirm the schedule is listed; the restore test is in R55.

scope.basis: Turn on the Railway backup schedule and record it; the restore test runs in the R55 smoke.
scope.risk: Low.

requirements.text: Keystroke < 16 ms; doc open < 50 ms p95; cold load < 1 s p95 (gated)
requirements.short: cold load < 1 s; doc open < 50 ms
requirements.story: Typing, opening docs, and first load stay instant

requirements.text: Agent save → open editor < 300 ms p95 (gated); save ack < 100 ms (17 ms MEASURED, not gated)
requirements.story: An agent's save shows up in your open editor within 300 ms

requirements.text: Cookie HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax set explicitly; CSP script-src 'self'; nosniff on /_assets and downloads; Content-Disposition attachment on exports; snippets rendered as text nodes
requirements.story: Other sites can't use or steal your session

edit.why: ~40 LOC of tower-http header layers and cookie attributes.

build_test.why: One to two cycles of an integration test asserting each header.

verify.why: Covered by that test.

scope.basis: tower-http headers, explicit cookie attributes, one integration test asserting them.
scope.risk: Low.

requirements.text: Structured errors (9 codes incl. not_allowed)
requirements.story: Errors say exactly what went wrong

edit.why: ~80 LOC = 4, plus 2 choosing the error codes.

build_test.why: One cycle with a test per code, plus a fix.

verify.why: Covered by its tests.

scope.basis: Error enum → JSON with 9 codes, one test per code.
scope.risk: Low.

requirements.text: check.sh = CI; real-binary integration over HTTP + MCP incl. cross-account isolation, allowlist 403, security headers/cookie attrs, script cannot see .git or escape /docs, crash-state recovery (4 states + stale lock), script folder rename keeps per-document history, script mkdir of an empty dir is reported as dropped; Playwright e2e incl. continuous typing, dropped ack, agent save during in-flight save; Railway smoke (Google + Claude Code; decode a real token). Includes the real Railway smoke test (30 min).
requirements.story: Agents prove every behavior against the real system before calling it done

edit.why: Rust integration suite ~400 LOC at 20 LOC/min = 20; Playwright, 8 journeys, ~300 LOC at 25 LOC/min = 12; smoke checklist 5.

build_test.why: Integration: 4 cycles at 3 min = 12. Playwright: 8 journeys at ~1.5 min, run about twice with fixes = 21.

verify.why: Railway smoke: deploy ≈ 5, Google login, Claude Code OAuth, token decode, and a volume restore test ≈ 15. It waits on you to sign in.

scope.basis: Integration suite (isolation, allowlist, headers, .git hidden, crash states) 30 min; Playwright journeys (8) 30 min; real Railway smoke (deploy, Google login, Claude Code OAuth, decode token, restore test) 30 min.
scope.risk: Flaky end-to-end tests; the smoke test waits on you to sign in.

requirements.text: Bench gate: agent→editor, cold load
requirements.story: A speed regression fails the agent's build

edit.why: ~120 LOC at 25 LOC/min = 5, plus 5 building the timing harness.

build_test.why: Repeated runs to get past timing noise.

verify.why: The gate is the check.

scope.basis: Bench script timing agent save → SSE → editor update and cold load, against bench/budgets.json.
scope.risk: Timing noise needs repeated runs.
